operator_io_quirks: architect.id is TEXT PK but values are numeric strings '1'..'5'; bridge/mill.architect_id is INT FK to it — cross-type FK join (text vs integer affinity) must survive.
FK child column type (INT) contradicts parent PK type (TEXT): fill_foreign_keys_consistently copies parent values verbatim, so INT column receives text '1'..'5'.
All columns notnull=0, no CHECK, no UNIQUE indexes: nothing enforced at insert; PK uniqueness only via sample_fresh_primary_keys.
Tiny tables (5/15/6 rows): original_values sampling with rng.choices(k=min(5,len)) returns nearly the whole column; distinct counts 1-2 for gender/type/notes.
mill.notes has distinct=1 ('Molenechos (Dutch)') — String sampler will mostly reproduce one value plus contamination.
Names contain spaces, commas, parentheses, non-ASCII (Othée, Château, 'Iraqi, British'): String CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9() will not reproduce them; literal pool carries them.
bridge.location distinct=14 of 15 rows (one duplicate) — near-unique text; drop_unique_duplicates only applies to declared unique cols, none here.
length_meters/length_feet REAL, correlated (feet≈3.28*meters) but TS treats independently — no FD enforcement in step 1.
built_year INT but semantically a year (1840-1890); declared type 'INT' dispatches to Number, not Year fuzzer — no year template.
DDL uses backtick-quoted parent `architect` and double-quoted elsewhere; sqlite_master order architect,bridge,mill gives clean topological levels.
No views/triggers/indexes; empty clone is just 3 CREATE TABLEs.
Self-FK none; both FKs point to architect (level 0), bridge/mill level 1.
operator_ts_expectations: architect.id (TEXT PK, single-col): String sampler, max_l0=inf, p=0.2 → fresh random strings like 'aB3()' plus original '1'..'5'; PK dedup keeps first.
bridge/mill.architect_id: FK fill copies architect.id final values with replacement → text values into INT column; sqlite stores as text, joins still work.
bridge.id/mill.id INT PK: Number sampler scale=0, range [-1,1] ints, perturb ±1/±2 → tiny integer space, heavy PK collisions, few surviving rows.
length_meters/length_feet REAL: Number scale=0 (no args) → integers in [-1,1] perturbed ±0.01/±0.02, wildly implausible vs 74-121 meters.
built_year INT: Number scale=0 → values near -1..1, not 1800s; any query filtering built_year>1800 returns empty → FN.
name/location/nationality/gender/type/notes: String length default [0,20], CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9() → no commas, accents, or real names; contamination adds junk.
gender/type/notes distinct 1-2: String sampler with p=0.2 mostly returns the single original element → low diversity, ties common.
Table sizes: choose_table_sizes w.p. 0.5 rand_lin (30..230) or level-based (level0 1+30u, level1 x4 capped 2500) → architect may get 1-230 rows, bridge/mill up to 4x.
Known FN driver: Number fuzzer on length_meters/built_year produces implausible magnitudes, so range predicates (length>100, built_year between 1800 and 1900) select nothing.
Known FP driver: tiny PK integer space + FK copy from small parent → many duplicate/empty joins; COUNT/aggregate queries may coincidentally match.
String contamination (0.5 prob) can turn 'male' into 'maleXYZ' or 'ale', breaking equality predicates on gender/type.
No NOT NULL/CHECK: NULLs never inserted (samplers drop None), so IS NULL queries always empty → FN.
